title: A fierce battle starts between Lakshmana and Indrajit
introduction: A fierce battle of archery starts between Indrajit and Lakshmana. Indrajit strikes Lakshmana with seven arrows, Hanuma with ten arrows and Vibhishana with a hundred arrows/almost at the same time. In retaliation, Lakshmana strikes Indrajit with a multiple of arrows and Indrajit's armour breaks up into pieces. Indrajit, in response, strikes Lakshmana with a thousand arrows and breaks up Lakshmana's armour. A fierce fight ensues for a long time. Meanwhile, Vibhishana joins the battle-field, to relieve Lakshmana's fatigue.
closing: इतार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे आदिकाव्ये युद्धकाण्डे अष्टाशीतितमः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 88th chapter in Yuddha Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा रावणिः क्रोधमूर्चितः |
अब्रवीत् परुषं वाक्यं वेगेनाभ्युत्पपात च
verses.iast:
vibhīṣaṇavacaḥ śrutvā rāvaṇiḥ krodhamūrcitaḥ |
abravīt paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ vegenābhyutpapāta ca
verses.translation: Hearing the words of Vibhishana, Indrajit was excited with rage, spoke harsh words and rushed forward in fury.

verses.devanagari:
उद्यतायुधनिस्त्रिंशो रथे सुसमलंकृते |
कालाश्वयुक्ते महति स्थितः कालान्तकोपमः
महाप्रमाणमुद्यम्य विपुलं वेगवद्दृढम् |
धनुर्भीमं परामृश्य शरांश्चामित्रशातनान्
verses.iast:
udyatāyudhanistriṃśo rathe susamalaṅkṛte |
kālāśvayukte mahati sthitaḥ kālāntakopamaḥ
mahāpramāṇamudyamya vipulaṃ vegavaddṛḍham |
dhanurbhīmaṃ parāmṛśya śarāṃścāmitraśātanān
verses.translation: Indrajit was looking like Yama the lord of Death at the time of dissolution of the world, sitting in a well-decorated and distinguished chariot yoked with black horses, having upraised sword and weapons, raising a big terrific enormous strong and swift bow and laying hold of arrows which can torment the enemies.

glosses.meaning: looking like Yama the lord of Death at the time of dissolution of the world
and yoked uplifted weapons and sword

verses.devanagari:
तं ददर्श महेष्वासो रथस्थः समलंकृतः |
अलंकृतममित्रघ्नो राघवस्यानुजं बली
verses.iast:
taṃ dadarśa maheṣvāso rathasthaḥ samalaṅkṛtaḥ |
alaṅkṛtamamitraghno rāghavasyānujaṃ balī
verses.translation: The mighty the destroyer of adversaries, wielding a large bow, fully adorned, and seated in a chariot saw that Lakshmana who was embellished with his own splendor.

verses.devanagari:
हनुमत्पृष्ठमारूढमुदयस्थरविप्रभम् |
उवाचैनं सुसंरब्धः सौमित्रिं सविभीषणम्
तांश्च वानरशार्दूलान् पश्यध्वं मे पराक्रमम् |
verses.iast:
hanumatpṛṣṭhamārūḍhamudayastharaviprabham |
uvācainaṃ susaṃrabdhaḥ saumitriṃ savibhīṣaṇam
tāṃśca vānaraśārdūlān paśyadhvaṃ me parākramam |
verses.translation: Indrajit hurriedly spoke to those foremost of monkeys and to this Lakshmana, who ascended Hanuma's back with a splendor of the sun shining on Mount Udaya and also with Vibhishana as follows: "You behold my prowess now."

glosses.meaning: to those foremost of monkeys and
with a splendor of the sun shining on Udaya Mountain

verses.devanagari:
अद्य मत्कारुमुकोत्सृष्टं शरवर्षं दुरासदम्
मुक्तं वर्षमिवाकाशे धारयिष्यथ संयुगे |
verses.iast:
adya matkārumukotsṛṣṭaṃ śaravarṣaṃ durāsadam
muktaṃ varṣamivākāśe dhārayiṣyatha saṃyuge |
verses.translation: "Now, you can face an unconquerable stream of arrows, like rain, released in the sky, as discharged from my bow in the battle-field."

verses.devanagari:
अद्य वो मामका बाणा महाकार्मुकनिःसृताः
विधमिष्यन्ति गात्राणि तूलराशिमिवानलः |
verses.iast:
adya vo māmakā bāṇā mahākārmukaniḥsṛtāḥ
vidhamiṣyanti gātrāṇi tūlarāśimivānalaḥ |
verses.translation: "Today my arrows released from my large bow will destroy your bodies, as fire consumes a pile of cotton."

verses.devanagari:
तीक्षणसायकनिर्भिन्नान् शूलशक्त्यृष्टितोमरैः
अद्य वो गमयिष्यामि सर्वानेन यमक्षयम् |
verses.iast:
tīkṣaṇasāyakanirbhinnān śūlaśaktyṛṣṭitomaraiḥ
adya vo gamayiṣyāmi sarvānena yamakṣayam |
verses.translation: "Today, I will send all of you to the world of Yama the lord of Death, by piercing you with my sharp arrows and hurling the pikes, javelins and lances on you."

glosses.meaning: to the world of Yama the lord of Death
by hurling the pikes javelins and lances.

verses.devanagari:
सृजतः शरवर्षाणि क्षिप्रहस्तस्य संयुगे
जीमूतस्येव नदतः कः स्थास्यति ममाग्रतः |
verses.iast:
sṛjataḥ śaravarṣāṇi kṣiprahastasya saṃyuge
jīmūtasyeva nadataḥ kaḥ sthāsyati mamāgrataḥ |
verses.translation: "Who can stand before me, while I release streams of arrows with my swift-hand in battle, thundering like a cloud?"

verses.devanagari:
रात्रियुद्धे तदा पूर्वं वज्राशनिसमैः शरैः
शायितौ स्थो मया भूमौ विसंज्ञौ सपुरस्सरौ |
verses.iast:
rātriyuddhe tadā pūrvaṃ vajrāśanisamaiḥ śaraiḥ
śāyitau stho mayā bhūmau visañjJṇau sapurassarau |
verses.translation: "Earlier on that day, in a nocturnal battle, both of you along with Sugreeva and other followers, were made unconscious by my arrows which were like thunderbolts and tips of missiles as also you were made to fall down on the floor."

glosses.meaning: both of you along with your followers
which were like thunderbolts and tips of missiles

verses.devanagari:
स्मृतिर्न तेऽस्ति वा मन्ये व्यक्तं यातो यमक्षयम्
आशीविषसमं क्रुद्धं यन्माम् योद्धुमुपस्थितः |
verses.iast:
smṛtirna te'sti vā manye vyaktaṃ yāto yamakṣayam
āśīviṣasamaṃ kruddhaṃ yanmām yoddhumupasthitaḥ |
verses.translation: "Do you not have that remembrance? I presume clearly that you are on the road to Yama the lord of Death, since you have come to give battle to me, enraged as I am, like a venomous serpent."

glosses.meaning: to the abode of Yama the lord of Death

verses.devanagari:
तच्छ्रुत्वा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य गर्जितं राघवस्तदा
अभीतवदनः क्रुद्धो रावणिं वाक्यमब्रवीत् |
verses.iast:
tacchrutvā rākṣasendrasya garjitaṃ rāghavastadā
abhītavadanaḥ kruddho rāvaṇiṃ vākyamabravīt |
verses.translation: Enraged in hearing that roaring of Indrajit, Lakshmana then spoke the following words, with a courageous countenance.

verses.devanagari:
उक्तश्च दुर्गमः पारः कार्याणां राक्षस त्वया
कार्याणां कर्मणाम् पारं यो गच्छति स बुद्धिमान् |
verses.iast:
uktaśca durgamaḥ pāraḥ kāryāṇāṃ rākṣasa tvayā
kāryāṇāṃ karmaṇām pāraṃ yo gacchati sa buddhimān |
verses.translation: "O demon! It has been proclaimed by you about the successful conclusion of your tasks, eventhough it is difficult to achieve them. He alone is clever, whoever carries through his undertakings in practice."

glosses.meaning: eventhough it is difficult to achieve

verses.devanagari:
स त्वमर्थस्य हीनार्थो दुरवापस्य केनचित्
वाचा व्याहृत्य जानीषे कृतार्थोऽस्मिति दुर्मते |
verses.iast:
sa tvamarthasya hīnārtho duravāpasya kenacit
vācā vyāhṛtya jānīṣe kṛtārtho'smiti durmate |
verses.translation: "O evil-minded one! You are thinking that you have accomplished your end, by proclaiming through word alone, the achievement of your end, which is difficult to attain for anyone, though you, as such, lack in capacity to achieve your purpose."

glosses.meaning: though you as such are lacking in capacity to achieve your end.

verses.devanagari:
अंतर्धानगतेनाजौ यस्त्वया चरितस्तदा
तस्कराचरितो मार्गः नैष वीरनिषेवितः |
verses.iast:
antardhānagatenājau yastvayā caritastadā
taskarācarito mārgaḥ naiṣa vīraniṣevitaḥ |
verses.translation: "The path, which was followed on that day by you, becoming invisible in the battle-field, is the one trodden by thieves and is not the path followed by valiant ones."

glosses.meaning: is to be followed by thieves
is not to be followed by valiant ones.

verses.devanagari:
यथा बाणपथं प्राप्य स्थितोऽस्मि तव राक्षस
दर्शयस्वाद्य तत्तेजो वाचा त्वं किं विकत्थसे |
verses.iast:
yathā bāṇapathaṃ prāpya sthito'smi tava rākṣasa
darśayasvādya tattejo vācā tvaṃ kiṃ vikatthase |
verses.translation: "O demon! Having reached the range of your arrows, I am standing before you. Therefore show your prowess today. Why should you brag with your words?

glosses.meaning: within the range of your arrows

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्तो धनुर्भीमं परामृश्य महाबलः
ससर्ज निशितान् बाणानिंद्रजित् समितिञ्जयः |
verses.iast:
evamukto dhanurbhīmaṃ parāmṛśya mahābalaḥ
sasarja niśitān bāṇānindrajit samitiJṇjayaḥ |
verses.translation: Hearing those words, the mighty Indrajit, victorious in battle, reaching his terrific bow, released sharp arrows from it.

verses.devanagari:
तेन सृष्टा महावेगाः शराः सर्पविषोपमाः
संप्राप्य लक्ष्मणं पेतुः श्वसन्त इव पन्नगाः |
verses.iast:
tena sṛṣṭā mahāvegāḥ śarāḥ sarpaviṣopamāḥ
samprāpya lakṣmaṇaṃ petuḥ śvasanta iva pannagāḥ |
verses.translation: Duly reaching Lakshmana, the arrows released by Indrajit, which rushed with great speed and were as deadly as the venom of serpents, fell like the hissing of snakes.

glosses.meaning: and were deadly as the venom of serpents

verses.devanagari:
शरैरतिमहावेगै र्वेगवान् रावणात्मजः
सौमित्रिमिन्द्रजिद्युद्धे विव्याध शुभलक्षणम् |
verses.iast:
śarairatimahāvegai rvegavān rāvaṇātmajaḥ
saumitrimindrajidyuddhe vivyādha śubhalakṣaṇam |
verses.translation: The swift Indrajit, the son of Ravana, with his arrows of very great velocity, in that battle, struck Lakshmana who was endowed with auspicious body-marks.

glosses.meaning: who was endowed with auspicious body marks.

verses.devanagari:
स शरैरतिविद्धाङ्गो रुधिरेण समुक्षितः
शुशुभे लक्ष्मणः श्रीमान्विधूम इव पावकः |
verses.iast:
sa śarairatividdhāṇ^go rudhireṇa samukṣitaḥ
śuśubhe lakṣmaṇaḥ śrīmānvidhūma iva pāvakaḥ |
verses.translation: That glorious Lakshmana, drenched in blood, with his body very much wounded by arrows, shone like a smokeless flame.

glosses.meaning: with his body very much wounded

verses.devanagari:
इन्द्रजित्त्वात्मनः कर्म प्रसमीक्ष्याभिगम्य च
निनद्य सुमहानादमितं वचनमब्रवीत् |
verses.iast:
indrajittvātmanaḥ karma prasamīkṣyābhigamya ca
ninadya sumahānādamitaṃ vacanamabravīt |
verses.translation: Mulling over his own feat, Indrajit for his part, approaching Lakshmana and emitting an exceedingly loud roar, spoke the following words:

verses.devanagari:
पत्रिण शितधारास्ते शरा मत्कार्मुकच्युताः
आदास्यन्तेऽद्य सौमित्रे जीवितं जीवितान्तकाः |
verses.iast:
patriṇa śitadhārāste śarā matkārmukacyutāḥ
ādāsyante'dya saumitre jīvitaṃ jīvitāntakāḥ |
verses.translation: "The sharp-edged and deadly arrows, with their wings, released from my bow, will now take your life, O Lakshmana!"

verses.devanagari:
अद्य गोमायुसंघाश्च श्येनसंघाश्च लक्ष्मण
गृध्राश्च निपतन्तु त्वां गतासुं निहतं मया |
verses.iast:
adya gomāyusaṅghāśca śyenasaṅghāśca lakṣmaṇa
gṛdhrāśca nipatantu tvāṃ gatāsuṃ nihataṃ mayā |
verses.translation: "O Lakshmana! Let a number of Jackals, multitude of hawks and vultures descend upon you, when struck down by me, you are dead."

verses.devanagari:
क्षत्रबन्धुं सदानार्यं रामः परमदुर्मतिः
भक्तं भ्रातरमद्यैव त्वां द्रख्यति हतं मया |
verses.iast:
kṣatrabandhuṃ sadānāryaṃ rāmaḥ paramadurmatiḥ
bhaktaṃ bhrātaramadyaiva tvāṃ drakhyati hataṃ mayā |
verses.translation: "The exceedingly evil-minded Rama now itself can see you, a mere kshatriya (military class only for a name sake), ever ignoble and his devoted brother, killed by me."

glosses.meaning: a mere kshatriya (military class only for a name-sake)

verses.devanagari:
विस्रस्तकवचं भूमौ व्यपविद्धशरासनम्
हृतोत्तमाङ्गं सौमित्रे त्वामद्य निहतम् मया |
verses.iast:
visrastakavacaṃ bhūmau vyapaviddhaśarāsanam
hṛtottamāṇ^gaṃ saumitre tvāmadya nihatam mayā |
verses.translation: "O Lakshmana! Rama will see you, struck down by me today, with your armour dropped down, bow thrown about and head dismantled."

verses.devanagari:
इति ब्रुवाणम् संक्रुद्धं परुषं रावणात्मजम्
हेतुमद्वाक्यमर्थज्ञो लक्ष्मणः प्रत्युवाच ह |
verses.iast:
iti bruvāṇam saṅkruddhaṃ paruṣaṃ rāvaṇātmajam
hetumadvākyamarthajJṇo lakṣmaṇaḥ pratyuvāca ha |
verses.translation: Lakshmana, understanding the sense of the word, replied in the following logical words to the enraged Indrajit thus speaking harshly.

glosses.meaning: understanding the sense of the word

verses.devanagari:
वाग्बलं त्यज दुर्भद्धे क्रूरकर्मासि राक्षस
अथ कस्माद्वदस्येतत्संपादय सुकर्मणा |
verses.iast:
vāgbalaṃ tyaja durbhaddhe krūrakarmāsi rākṣasa
atha kasmādvadasyetatsampādaya sukarmaṇā |
verses.translation: "O evil-minded one! Give up strength of speech in your empty words. O demons! You are doing cruel acts. Why do you indulge in such idle talk? Make it active with your good work."

verses.devanagari:
अकृत्वा कत्थसे कर्म किमर्थमिह राक्षस
कुरु तत्कर्म येनाहं श्रद्दध्यां तव कत्थनम् |
verses.iast:
akṛtvā katthase karma kimarthamiha rākṣasa
kuru tatkarma yenāhaṃ śraddadhyāṃ tava katthanam |
verses.translation: "O demon! Without performing that act, why do you boast yourself here? Perform that act by which I can believe your brag."

verses.devanagari:
अनुक्त्वा परुषं वाक्यं किंचिदप्यनवक्षिपन्
अविकत्थन् वधिष्यामि त्वां पश्य पुरुषाधम |
verses.iast:
anuktvā paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ kiñcidapyanavakṣipan
avikatthan vadhiṣyāmi tvāṃ paśya puruṣādhama |
verses.translation: "O the worst of persons! Without speaking even a few harsh words, without abusing you and without bragging myself, Lo! I will kill you."

verses.devanagari:
इत्युक्त्वा पञ्च नाराचानाकर्णापूरितान् शरान्
विजघान महावेगाल्लक्ष्मणो राक्षसोरसि |
verses.iast:
ityuktvā paJṇca nārācānākarṇāpūritān śarān
vijaghāna mahāvegāllakṣmaṇo rākṣasorasi |
verses.translation: Thus speaking, Lakshmana stretching five steel arrows upto the ear, dug them into the demon's chest with a great speed.

glosses.meaning: stretching five steel arrows up to the ear

verses.devanagari:
सुपत्रवाजिता बाणा ज्वलिता इव पन्नगाः
नैरृतोरस्यभासन्त सवितू रश्मयो यथा |
verses.iast:
supatravājitā bāṇā jvalitā iva pannagāḥ
nairṛtorasyabhāsanta savitū raśmayo yathā |
verses.translation: The arrows, blazing like serpents and feathered with fine plumes, shone like sun-rays in that demon's chest.

verses.devanagari:
स शरैराहतस्तेन सरोषो रावणात्मजः
सुप्रयुक्तैस्त्रिभिर्बाणैः प्रतिविव्याध लक्ष्मणम् |
verses.iast:
sa śarairāhatastena saroṣo rāvaṇātmajaḥ
suprayuktaistribhirbāṇaiḥ prativivyādha lakṣmaṇam |
verses.translation: Struck with arrows by Lakshmana, that enraged Indrajit pierced in return three arrows well-directed towards Lakshmana.

verses.devanagari:
स बभूव महाभीमो नरराक्षससिंहयोः
विमर्दस्तुमुलो युद्धे परस्परजयैषिणोः |
verses.iast:
sa babhūva mahābhīmo nararākṣasasiṃhayoḥ
vimardastumulo yuddhe parasparajayaiṣiṇoḥ |
verses.translation: That fight between Lakshmana, the foremost among men and Indrajit, the formost among demons, who wished to conquer one over the other in battle, was most terrific and tumultuous.

glosses.meaning: between Lakshmana the foremost of men and Indrajit the foremost of demns
who wished to conquer one over the other

verses.devanagari:
उभौ हि बलसंपन्नावुभौ विक्रमशालिनौ
उभौ परमदुर्जेयावतुल्यबलतेजसौ |
verses.iast:
ubhau hi balasampannāvubhau vikramaśālinau
ubhau paramadurjeyāvatulyabalatejasau |
verses.translation: Both were endowed with strength. Both were distinguished for their prowess. Both were exceedingly difficult to conquer and peerless in strength and courage.

glosses.meaning: were exceedingly difficult to conquer atulya balatejasau = and peerless in strength and courage.

verses.devanagari:
युयुधाते तदा वीरौ ग्रहाविव नभोगतौ
बलवृत्राविवाभीतौ युधि तौ दुष्पृधर्षणौ |
verses.iast:
yuyudhāte tadā vīrau grahāviva nabhogatau
balavṛtrāvivābhītau yudhi tau duṣpṛdharṣaṇau |
verses.translation: Those two heroes, who were difficult to overcome in battle, fought at that moment like two plants figuring in the sky and like Indra and Vritra, the demon.

verses.devanagari:
युयुधाते महात्मानौ तदा केसरिणाविव
बहूनवष्^इजन्तौ हि मार्गणौघानवस्थितौ |
नरराक्षसमुख्यौ तौ प्रहृष्टावभ्ययुध्यताम्
verses.iast:
yuyudhāte mahātmānau tadā kesariṇāviva
bahūnavaṣ^ijantau hi mārgaṇaughānavasthitau |
nararākṣasamukhyau tau prahṛṣṭāvabhyayudhyatām
verses.translation: Then, the two warriors, who were engaged in releasing several streams of arrows, fought like two lions. Lakshmana the foremost among humans and Indrajit the foremost among demons fought with rejoice.

glosses.meaning: foremost of human being and demons

verses.devanagari:
ततश्श्रान् दाशरथिः संधायामित्रकर्षणः |
ससर्ज राक्षसेन्द्रय कृद्धः सर्प इव श्वसन्
verses.iast:
tataśśrān dāśarathiḥ sandhāyāmitrakarṣaṇaḥ |
sasarja rākṣasendraya kṛddhaḥ sarpa iva śvasan
verses.translation: Thereupon, Lakshmana the tormentator of enemies, fitting his arrows to his bow, released arrows on Indrajit, hissing like an enraged serpent.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य ज्यातलनिर्घोषं स श्रुत्वा राक्षसाधिपः |
विवर्णवदनो भूत्वा लक्ष्मणं समुदैक्षत
verses.iast:
tasya jyātalanirghoṣaṃ sa śrutvā rākṣasādhipaḥ |
vivarṇavadano bhūtvā lakṣmaṇaṃ samudaikṣata
verses.translation: Hearing the twang of the bow-string of Lakshmana, Indrajit the Chief of demons became pale-faced and fixed his gaze on Lakshmana.

glosses.meaning: the twang of the bow string

verses.devanagari:
विषण्णवदनं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसं रावणात्मजम् |
सौमित्रिं युद्धसंयुक्तं प्रत्युवाच विभीषणः
verses.iast:
viṣaṇṇavadanaṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasaṃ rāvaṇātmajam |
saumitriṃ yuddhasaṃyuktaṃ pratyuvāca vibhīṣaṇaḥ
verses.translation: Seeing Indrajit (the son of Ravana) pale-faced, Vibhishana spoke as follows to Lakshmana, who was fully absorbed in the fight.

glosses.meaning: who was absorbed in the fight.

verses.devanagari:
निमित्तान्युपपश्यामि यान्यस्मिन् रावणात्मजे |
त्वर तेन महाबाहो भग्न एष न संशयः
verses.iast:
nimittānyupapaśyāmi yānyasmin rāvaṇātmaje |
tvara tena mahābāho bhagna eṣa na saṃśayaḥ
verses.translation: "O the long-armed Lakshmana! I infer on the strength of the indications which I see in Indrajit, that he is disappointed. There is no doubt about it. Make haste."

verses.devanagari:
ततस्संधाय सौमित्रिः शरानाशीविषोपमान् |
मुमोच निशितांस्तस्मिन् सर्पानिव विषोल्बणान्
verses.iast:
tatassandhāya saumitriḥ śarānāśīviṣopamān |
mumoca niśitāṃstasmin sarpāniva viṣolbaṇān
verses.translation: Thereupon, fitting to his bow sharp arrows, resembling poisonous snakes, Lakshmana discharged those arrows which looked like serpents full of venom to him.

glosses.meaning: which looked like serpents full of venom

verses.devanagari:
शक्राशनिसमस्पर्शैर्लक्षमणेनाहतः शरैः |
मुहूर्तमभवन्मूढः सर्वसंक्षुभितेन्द्रियः
verses.iast:
śakrāśanisamasparśairlakṣamaṇenāhataḥ śaraiḥ |
muhūrtamabhavanmūḍhaḥ sarvasaṅkṣubhitendriyaḥ
verses.translation: Hit by Lakshmana with arrows, which invaded all his senses, like the hit of Indra's thunderbolt, Indrajit became stupefied for a moment.

glosses.meaning: like the painful touching of Indra's thunderbolt

verses.devanagari:
उपलभ्य मुहूर्तेन संज्ञाम् प्रत्यागतेन्द्रियः |
ददर्शावस्थितं वीरमाजौ दशरथात्मजम्
verses.iast:
upalabhya muhūrtena sañjJṇām pratyāgatendriyaḥ |
dadarśāvasthitaṃ vīramājau daśarathātmajam
verses.translation: Regaining his consciousness within a moment, with his senses restored, that Indrajit saw the valiant Lakshmana engaged in the battle.

verses.devanagari:
सोऽभिचक्राम सौमित्रिं रोषात्संरक्तलोचनः |
अब्रवीछैनमासाद्य पुनः स परुषं वचः
verses.iast:
so'bhicakrāma saumitriṃ roṣātsaṃraktalocanaḥ |
abravīchainamāsādya punaḥ sa paruṣaṃ vacaḥ
verses.translation: With blood-red eyes in anger, Indrajit walked towards Lakshmana. Approaching Lakshmana, he again spoke the following harsh words to him:

verses.devanagari:
किं न स्मरसि तद्युद्धे प्रथमे यत्पराक्रमम् |
निबद्धस्त्वं सह भ्रात्रा यदा भुवि विचेष्टसे
verses.iast:
kiṃ na smarasi tadyuddhe prathame yatparākramam |
nibaddhastvaṃ saha bhrātrā yadā bhuvi viceṣṭase
verses.translation: "Don't you remember my prowess in the first encounter, when you along with your brother, was bound by me and you wriggled on the floor?"

verses.devanagari:
युवां खलु महायुद्धे शक्रानिसमैः शरैः |
शायितौ प्रथमम् भूमौ विसंज्ञौ सपुरःसरौ
verses.iast:
yuvāṃ khalu mahāyuddhe śakrānisamaiḥ śaraiḥ |
śāyitau prathamam bhūmau visañjJṇau sapuraḥsarau
verses.translation: "At first, both of you along with your foremost warriors in a major encounter, were indeed laid down unconscious on the ground, by my arrows which were equal to Indra's thunderbolt."

glosses.meaning: which were equal to Indra's thunderbolt.

verses.devanagari:
स्मृतिर्वा नास्ति ते मन्ये व्यक्तं वा यमसादनम् |
गन्तुमिच्छसि यन्मां त्वमाधर्षयितुमिच्छसि
verses.iast:
smṛtirvā nāsti te manye vyaktaṃ vā yamasādanam |
gantumicchasi yanmāṃ tvamādharṣayitumicchasi
verses.translation: "The fact that you desire to attack me means that either the remembrance of it no longer exists in you or I presume you desire to go clearly to the abode of Yama the lord of Death."

glosses.meaning: to the abode of Yama the lord of Death

verses.devanagari:
यदि ते प्रथमे युद्धे न दृष्टो मत्पराक्रमः |
अद्य त्वां दर्शयिष्यामि तिषेदानीं व्यवस्थितः
verses.iast:
yadi te prathame yuddhe na dṛṣṭo matparākramaḥ |
adya tvāṃ darśayiṣyāmi tiṣedānīṃ vyavasthitaḥ
verses.translation: "If my prowess was not witnessed by you in the first encounter, I will show it today. Stand ready for it now."

glosses.meaning: If my prowess was not witnessed

verses.devanagari:
इत्युक्त्वा सप्तभिर्बाणैरभिविव्याध लक्ष्मणम् |
दशभिस्तु हनूमन्तं तीक्षणधारैः शरोत्तमैः
verses.iast:
ityuktvā saptabhirbāṇairabhivivyādha lakṣmaṇam |
daśabhistu hanūmantaṃ tīkṣaṇadhāraiḥ śarottamaiḥ
verses.translation: Thus speaking, he struck Lakshmana with seven arrows and Hanuma with ten excellent sharp-edged arrows.

verses.devanagari:
ततः शरशतेनैव सुप्रयुक्तेन वीर्यवान् |
क्रोधाद्द्विगुणसंरब्धो निर्बिभेद विभीषणम्
verses.iast:
tataḥ śaraśatenaiva suprayuktena vīryavān |
krodhāddviguṇasaṃrabdho nirbibheda vibhīṣaṇam
verses.translation: Then, the valiant Idnrajit with anger and with twice as much vehemence, wounded Vibhishana with a hundred well-aimed arrows.

glosses.meaning: and with twice as much vehemence

verses.devanagari:
तद्दृष्ट्वेन्द्रजिता कर्म कृतं रामानुजस्तदा |
अचिन्तयित्वा प्रहसन्नैतत्किंचिदिति ब्रुवन्
मुमोच च शरान् घोरान् संगृह्य नरपुंगवः |
अभीतवदनः क्रुद्धो रावनिं लक्ष्मणो युधि
verses.iast:
taddṛṣṭvendrajitā karma kṛtaṃ rāmānujastadā |
acintayitvā prahasannaitatkiñciditi bruvan
mumoca ca śarān ghorān saṅgṛhya narapuṅgavaḥ |
abhītavadanaḥ kruddho rāvaniṃ lakṣmaṇo yudhi
verses.translation: Seeing that feat accomplished by Indrajit, yet disregarding it, deriding it by saying "This is noting" and taking up terrific arrows, the fearless and enraged Lakshmana the younger brother of Rama and foremost among men, then discharged them against Indrajit in battle.

glosses.meaning: and taking ghoraan sharaan = terrific arrows

verses.devanagari:
नैवं रणगताः शूराः प्रहरन्ति निशाचर |
लघुवश्चाल्पवीर्याश्च शरा हीमे सुखास्तव
verses.iast:
naivaṃ raṇagatāḥ śūrāḥ praharanti niśācara |
laghuvaścālpavīryāśca śarā hīme sukhāstava
verses.translation: "O demon! Heroes who come to battle do not strike like this. These arrows of yours are light, weak and mild indeed."

verses.devanagari:
नैवं शूरास्तु युध्यन्ते समरे जयकांक्षिणः |
इत्येवं तं ब्रुवन् धन्वी शरैरभिववर्ष ह
verses.iast:
naivaṃ śūrāstu yudhyante samare jayakāṅkṣiṇaḥ |
ityevaṃ taṃ bruvan dhanvī śarairabhivavarṣa ha
verses.translation: "Warriors, who wish to win in battle, do not fight like this." Thus speaking, Lakshmana the wielder of a bow, streamed forth arrows on him.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य बाणैः सुविध्वस्तं कवचं काञ्चनं महत् |
व्यशीर्यत रथोपस्थे ताराजालमिवाम्बरात्
verses.iast:
tasya bāṇaiḥ suvidhvastaṃ kavacaṃ kāJṇcanaṃ mahat |
vyaśīryata rathopasthe tārājālamivāmbarāt
verses.translation: A large golden armour, broken to pieces by Lakshmana's arrows, slipped down in the middle of chariot, like a cob-web of stars falling from the sky.

glosses.meaning: in the middle of his chariot

verses.devanagari:
विधूतवर्मा नाराचैर्बभूव स कृतव्रणः |
इन्द्रजित्समरे वीरः प्रत्यूषे भानुमानिव
verses.iast:
vidhūtavarmā nārācairbabhūva sa kṛtavraṇaḥ |
indrajitsamare vīraḥ pratyūṣe bhānumāniva
verses.translation: The valiant Indrajit, with his armour disheveled by the steel arrows, was wounded in battle and looked like the sun at dawn.

verses.devanagari:
ततः शरसहस्रेण संक्रुद्धो रावणात्मजः |
बिभेद समरे वीरो लक्ष्मणं भीमविद्रमः
verses.iast:
tataḥ śarasahasreṇa saṅkruddho rāvaṇātmajaḥ |
bibheda samare vīro lakṣmaṇaṃ bhīmavidramaḥ
verses.translation: Thereafter, the valiant Indrajit of terrific prowess was enraged and wounded Lakshmana with a thousand arrows in battle.

verses.devanagari:
व्यशीर्यत महद्दिव्यं कवचम् लक्ष्मणस्य तु |
कृतप्रतिकृतान्योन्यं बभूवतुरभिद्रुतौ
verses.iast:
vyaśīryata mahaddivyaṃ kavacam lakṣmaṇasya tu |
kṛtapratikṛtānyonyaṃ babhūvaturabhidrutau
verses.translation: The large celestial armour of Lakshmana broke into pieces. The two warriors vied with each other in offence and retaliation in their attack.

glosses.meaning: with each other in offence and retaliation

verses.devanagari:
अभीक्षणम् निःश्वसन्तौ तौ युध्येतां तुमुलं युधि |
शरसंकृत्तसर्वाङ्गौ सर्वतो रुधिरोक्षितौ
verses.iast:
abhīkṣaṇam niḥśvasantau tau yudhyetāṃ tumulaṃ yudhi |
śarasaṅkṛttasarvāṇ^gau sarvato rudhirokṣitau
verses.translation: Those two warriors, with their entire bodies lacerated in combat, smeared with blood all around and breathing heavily, fought the battle tumultuously.

glosses.meaning: with all their limbs got lacerated

verses.devanagari:
सुदीर्घकालं तौ वीरावन्योन्यं निशितैः शरैः |
ततक्षतुर्महत्मानौ रणकर्मविशारदौ
verses.iast:
sudīrghakālaṃ tau vīrāvanyonyaṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ |
tatakṣaturmahatmānau raṇakarmaviśāradau
verses.translation: Thos mighty warriors, skilled in warfare, were cutting through each other, for a long time, with sharp arrows.

verses.devanagari:
बभूवतुश्चात्मजये यतौ भीमपराक्रमौ |
तौ शरौघै स्तथाकीर्णौ निकृत्तकवचध्वजौ
सृजन्तौ रुधिरं चोष्णं जलं प्रस्रवणाविव |
verses.iast:
babhūvatuścātmajaye yatau bhīmaparākramau |
tau śaraughai stathākīrṇau nikṛttakavacadhvajau
sṛjantau rudhiraṃ coṣṇaṃ jalaṃ prasravaṇāviva |
verses.translation: Those two heroes f terrific prowess stay on strenuously trying to secure their own victory, covered as they were, all over with a multitude of arrows as also their armour and standards torn to pieces. They stood emitting hot blood, as two water-falls gushing hot water.

glosses.meaning: those two heroes of terrific prowess
their armour and standards torn to pieces

verses.devanagari:
शरवर्षं ततो घोरं मुञ्चतोर्भीमनिःस्वनम्
सासारयोरिवाकाशे नीलयोः कालेमेघयोः |
तयोरथ महान् कालो व्यतीयाद्युध्यमानयोः
न च तौ युद्धवैमुख्यं श्रमं चाप्युपजग्मतुः |
verses.iast:
śaravarṣaṃ tato ghoraṃ muJṇcatorbhīmaniḥsvanam
sāsārayorivākāśe nīlayoḥ kālemeghayoḥ |
tayoratha mahān kālo vyatīyādyudhyamānayoḥ
na ca tau yuddhavaimukhyaṃ śramaṃ cāpyupajagmatuḥ |
verses.translation: Much of a time lapsed while the two warriors fought loosing terrific stream of arrows, then with an awful clamour, like two dark destructive clouds raining from the sky. They neither trned their back from the battle, nor experienced any fatigue.

glosses.meaning: turned their back from the battle

verses.devanagari:
अस्त्राण्यस्त्रविदां श्रेष्ठौ दर्शयन्त् पुनः पुनः
शरानुच्चावचाकारानन्तरिक्षे बबन्धतुः |
verses.iast:
astrāṇyastravidāṃ śreṣṭhau darśayant punaḥ punaḥ
śarānuccāvacākārānantarikṣe babandhatuḥ |
verses.translation: Displaying their missiles again and again, the two warriors, who were excellent among those skilled in the use missiles, fastened a net work of arrows both large and small, in the sky.

glosses.meaning: among those skilled in the use of missiles
of both large and small shapes

verses.devanagari:
व्यपेतदोषमस्यन्तौ लघु चित्रं च सुष्ठु च
उभौ तु तुमुलं घोरं चक्रतुर्नरराक्षसौ |
verses.iast:
vyapetadoṣamasyantau laghu citraṃ ca suṣṭhu ca
ubhau tu tumulaṃ ghoraṃ cakraturnararākṣasau |
verses.translation: Loosing their arrows faultlessly, gracefully and easily in a wonderful way, both the man and the demon carried on a tumultuous and terrific war.

glosses.meaning: both the man and the demon

verses.devanagari:
तयोः पृथक् पृथग्भीमः शुश्रुवे तुमुलः स्वनः
सुघोरयोर्निःस्वनतोर्गगने मेघयोरिव |
verses.iast:
tayoḥ pṛthak pṛthagbhīmaḥ śuśruve tumulaḥ svanaḥ
sughorayorniḥsvanatorgagane meghayoriva |
verses.translation: Their terrific and tumultuous sound could be heard one by one repeatedly. That sound created a tremble in people, like a violent thunder-storm.

verses.devanagari:
तयोः स भ्राजते शब्दस्तथा समरयत्तयोः
सुघोरयोर्निःस्वनतोर्गगने मेघयोरिव |
verses.iast:
tayoḥ sa bhrājate śabdastathā samarayattayoḥ
sughorayorniḥsvanatorgagane meghayoriva |
verses.translation: That clamour of those two warriors, who were engaged thus in that martial act, resembled the rumbling of two dreadful thundering clouds in the sky.

glosses.meaning: who were engaged thus in that martial act

verses.devanagari:
सुवर्णपुङ्खैर्नाराचैर्बलवन्तौ कृतव्रणौ
प्रसुस्रुवाते रुधिरं कीर्तिमन्तौ जये धृतौ |
verses.iast:
suvarṇapuṇ^khairnārācairbalavantau kṛtavraṇau
prasusruvāte rudhiraṃ kīrtimantau jaye dhṛtau |
verses.translation: Those two mighty and glorious warriors, who were determined to gain victory over one another, wounded with golden-shafted steel arrows, were profusely giving out blood.

glosses.meaning: those two mighty and glorious warriors

verses.devanagari:
ते गात्रयोर्निपतिता रुक्मपुङ्खाः शरा युधि
असृग्दिग्धा विनिष्पेतुर्विविशुर्धरणीतलम् |
verses.iast:
te gātrayornipatitā rukmapuṇ^khāḥ śarā yudhi
asṛgdigdhā viniṣpeturviviśurdharaṇītalam |
verses.translation: Fallen on their limbs, the golden-shafted arrows, dropped on the battle-field, smeared with blood and pierced into the surface of the earth.

verses.devanagari:
अन्ये सुनिशितैः शस्त्रैराकाशे संजघट्टिरे
बभञ्जुश्चिच्छिदुश्चैव तयोर्बाणाः सहस्रशः |
verses.iast:
anye suniśitaiḥ śastrairākāśe sañjaghaṭṭire
babhaJṇjuścicchiduścaiva tayorbāṇāḥ sahasraśaḥ |
verses.translation: Some more arrows released by those two warriors clashed in thousands with sharp weapons in the sky and shattered and tore them.

verses.devanagari:
स बभूव रणे घोरस्तयोर्बाणमयश्चयः
अग्निभ्यामिव दीप्ताभ्यां सत्रे कुशमयश्चयः |
verses.iast:
sa babhūva raṇe ghorastayorbāṇamayaścayaḥ
agnibhyāmiva dīptābhyāṃ satre kuśamayaścayaḥ |
verses.translation: The terrific pile of arrows in battle appeared like a mass of sacred Kusha grass by the side of two blazing fires at a sacrifice.

glosses.meaning: like a mass of sacred Kusha grass
by the side of two blazing fires

verses.devanagari:
तयोः कृतव्रणौ देहौ शुशुभाते महात्मनोः
सुपुष्पाविव निष्पत्रौ वने किंशुकशाल्मली |
verses.iast:
tayoḥ kṛtavraṇau dehau śuśubhāte mahātmanoḥ
supuṣpāviva niṣpatrau vane kiṃśukaśālmalī |
verses.translation: The wounded bodies of those two mighty warriors shone like Kimshuka and Shalmali (silk-cotton) trees in full blossom, deprived of leaves.

verses.devanagari:
चक्रतुस्तुमुलं घोरं संनिपातं मुहुर्मुहुः
इन्द्रजिल्लक्ष्मणश्चैव परस्परजयैषिणौ |
verses.iast:
cakratustumulaṃ ghoraṃ saṃnipātaṃ muhurmuhuḥ
indrajillakṣmaṇaścaiva parasparajayaiṣiṇau |
verses.translation: Indrajit and Lakshmana who were time and again wishing to attain victory one over the other, carried out tumultuous and terrific battle.

glosses.meaning: who were time and again wishing to attain victory one over the other

verses.devanagari:
लक्ष्मणो रावणिं युद्धे रावणिश्चापि लक्ष्मणम्
अन्योन्यं तावभिघ्नन्तौ न श्रमं प्रतिपद्यताम् |
verses.iast:
lakṣmaṇo rāvaṇiṃ yuddhe rāvaṇiścāpi lakṣmaṇam
anyonyaṃ tāvabhighnantau na śramaṃ pratipadyatām |
verses.translation: In the combat, Lakshmana was striking Indrajit and Indrajit too was striking Lakshmana. Both of them were striking each other and did not experience any weariness.

verses.devanagari:
बाणजालैः शरीरस्थैरवगाढैस्तरस्विनौ
शुशुभाते महाविर्यौ प्ररूढाविव पर्वतौ |
verses.iast:
bāṇajālaiḥ śarīrasthairavagāḍhaistarasvinau
śuśubhāte mahāviryau prarūḍhāviva parvatau |
verses.translation: With a multitude of arrows dug deep into their bodies, those two warriors, of great prowess and swiftness, shone like two mountains shooting forth plants from them.

glosses.meaning: those two warriors of great prowess and swiftness

verses.devanagari:
ततो रुधिरस्तिक्तानि संवृतानि शरैर्भृशम्
बभ्राजुः सर्वगात्राणि ज्वलन्त इव पावकाः |
verses.iast:
tato rudhirastiktāni saṃvṛtāni śarairbhṛśam
babhrājuḥ sarvagātrāṇi jvalanta iva pāvakāḥ |
verses.translation: At that time, all their limbs, dampened with blood and thickly covered with arrows shone very much like blazing fires.

verses.devanagari:
तयोरथ महान् कालो व्यतीयाद्युध्यमानयोः
न च तौ युद्धवैमुख्यं श्रमं चाप्यभिजग्मतुः |
verses.iast:
tayoratha mahān kālo vyatīyādyudhyamānayoḥ
na ca tau yuddhavaimukhyaṃ śramaṃ cāpyabhijagmatuḥ |
verses.translation: A lot of time lapsed in the meanwhile past the two warriors. They neither turned their back from the battle nor experienced any fatigue.

glosses.meaning: in the meanwhile past between them
turned their back from the battle

verses.devanagari:
अथ समरपरिश्रमं निहन्तुं |
समरमुखेष्वजितस्य लक्ष्मणस्य |
प्रियहितमुपपादयन्महात्मा |
समरमु पेत्य विभीषणोऽवतस्थे
verses.iast:
atha samarapariśramaṃ nihantuṃ |
samaramukheṣvajitasya lakṣmaṇasya |
priyahitamupapādayanmahātmā |
samaramu petya vibhīṣaṇo'vatasthe
verses.translation: Then, to relieve martial weariness of Lakshmana, who did not experience defeat in any facet of war, the great-souled Vibhishana, offering agreeable and salutary words, took up his position, on reaching the battle-field.

glosses.meaning: who did not know defeat in any facet of war
